title: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yose bar Chanina.

Hyman writes: Of this great Amora, whose sayings and halakhot fill the Babylonian and Jerusalem Talmuds, we do not know who his father Rabbi Chanina was. It is very difficult to say that Rabbi Chanina bar Chama was his father, for we never find him speaking in the name of his father Rabbi Chanina. But this we know clearly: he was among the greatest students of Rabbi Yochanan, and Rabbi Yochanan ordained him, as stated explicitly in [Sanhedrin 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.30b.2-3), which relates that his colleague Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim tried unsuccessfully to arrange his ordination. One day he was sitting before Rabbi Yochanan, who said to them, “Is there anyone who knows whether the halakhah follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah or not?” Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said to him, “This one (Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina) knows.” He said to him, “Let him say it.” He said to him, “Let the master ordain him first.” He ordained him, and said to him, “My son, say it” — since you have gone up, you shall not go down.

Likewise we find that he taught before Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yochanan praised him, as in [Me’ilah 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Meilah.16b.2-3); he raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan, as in [Yevamot 27b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.27b.8); and in [Bava Kamma 112b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.112b.4-5), Rabbi Yochanan wondered at it — Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina accepted it from him; and in [Kiddushin 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.43b.8-9), Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina said: What is Rabbi Yochanan’s reason?

Likewise we find in aggadah, [Bava Metzia 85b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.85b.8), that Rabbi Zeira said: Last night Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina appeared to me (in a dream); I said to him, “Near whom are you set?” He said to me, “Near Rabbi Yochanan.”

In [Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sanhedrin.3.9.22), Rabbi Yonatan was sitting and asking, “Is there anyone who has heard whether the halakhah follows Rabbi Nathan?” Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina said to him, “Here is Rabbi Shimon ben Yakim.” “Let him come up.” Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina meant only to raise Rabbi Shimon ben Yakim up, because he was a great man. Hyman understands this as ordaining him.

Hyman reports that Dor Dor ve-Dorshav (דו״ד), part 3, end of chapter 8, note 15, took this as evidence that Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina was not a student of Rabbi Yochanan. It treats the account of Rabbi Yochanan ordaining him in Babylonian Talmud [Sanhedrin 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.30b.2-4) as corrupt and proposes a reading in line with the Jerusalem Talmud, in which Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim was ordained through Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. Hyman replies that the scholar overlooked the fact that Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim was already a great man of the generation even in Rabbi Yochanan’s lifetime. He was Rabbi Elazar’s colleague, and both served as judges, as in Bava Kamma 117a in Hyman’s citation (compare [Bava Kamma 117b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.117b.6)).
And in Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:3, Rabbi Elazar addressed him as “my teacher.”

Hyman argues that in truth both were great men of the generation even in Rabbi Yochanan’s lifetime, and both were judges. [Bava Kamma 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.39a.13) explicitly says that Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina was a judge who delved into the merits of a case. Hyman proposes that a scribal error in the Jerusalem Talmud put Rabbi Yonatan in place of Rabbi Yochanan, since, he says, we never find that they sat before Rabbi Yonatan. Hyman insists that both stories are true: Rabbi Yochanan ordained them both, and they were all his students. He likewise considers Resh Lakish and Rabbi Elazar subordinate to Rabbi Yochanan, whom he describes as head of the whole generation after the deaths of Rav and Shmuel in Babylonia.

Likewise we find that he disagrees with Rabbi Yochanan in [Ketubot 84a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.84a.16), [Nazir 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.29a.5-6) and [Bava Kamma 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.39a.9-13).[^9]

In [Berakhot 40b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.40b.24), Hyman discusses a reading in which Rabbi Yitzchak cites Rabbi Yochanan, who cites Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim omits the first two names, and it seems that the words “some say” were needlessly deleted there. The plain sense is this: first several things are cited that Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, and afterward it was written “some say” that Rabbi Yitzchak too said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, apart from what Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov — but not that Rabbi Yochanan would speak in the name of his student Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. Hyman considers this clear.[^8]

Hyman continues: Now since Rabbi Yochanan lived very long, all his earliest students afterward became his student-colleagues, and after Rabbi Yochanan’s death his last students sat before his first students, as explained in the entries Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim and Rabbi Ami. So too with Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, who left the status of a student, and Rabbi Yochanan’s students received from him, as we shall explain below. Not only did he receive from Rabbi Yochanan, but he also received from Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, as in Yevamot 8:6, where he asked Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish; he spoke in his name, as in Moed Katan 3:4, folio 12b, Sanhedrin, beginning of chapter 8, and [Nazir 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.29a.6). As for the reading Hyman cites at Ketubot 49b, “Rabbi Ila’a said that Resh Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina” — Hyman considers it a scribal error and proposes “in the name of Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Chanina,” for so it is in Eruvin 11b.[^10][^11]

And in Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 4:8, Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Chanina was Resh Lakish’s teacher. Likewise in Sukkah 1:1, folio 3 [as supplied], Hyman considers it erroneous when it reads “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina,” and he proposes Rabbi Yudah son of Chanina, as in Eruvin 1:9 and Kilayim 4:2. Hyman considers it very likely that what we find in the Tosefta, end of Arakhin — “Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina said: Come and see how severe is the ‘dust’ of the Sabbatical year,” cited in his name in Arakhin 30 [no side supplied] and [Kiddushin 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.20a.16) — is a scribal error: the Tosefta had the abbreviation “Rabbi Y. son of Rabbi Chanina,” meaning Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Chanina, and from it was made Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, which spread from the Tosefta into the Gemara. Otherwise we would necessarily have to say, following the view of the [Tosafot in Nazir 29a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Nazir.29a.15.1), s.v. “hakhi garsinan” (ה״ג), that there was a Tanna named Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina.[^12]

Likewise, regarding the mention of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina at the beginning of Sifrei Devarim, Hyman writes: We have already explained that it should read Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi, as the saying is cited in [Arakhin 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.15a.14).[^13]
Likewise we find that he spoke in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as in Jerusalem Talmud Yoma, beginning of chapter 8, and in the name of Menachem Yotfayah, as in Sukkah 4:6.

In Dor Dor ve-Dorshav (דו״ד), part 3, end of chapter 8, Weiss suggests that Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina may first have served before Rabbi Chama, the father of Rabbi Hoshaya, since in Sheviit 2:2 he speaks in his name. Hyman rejects this as untrue. By that reasoning, he says, one could equally claim that he served before Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov, since he said several things in his name. Rabbi Chama, the father of Rabbi Hoshaya, is known to have lived in the time of Rabbi, so, Hyman concludes, Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina undoubtedly never saw him. Hyman says that the Zhitomir printing of the Jerusalem Talmud omits the entire saying cited by Weiss.

In [Nazir 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.42a.2-4) we find that Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina challenges the words of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika (the colleague of Rav Pappa). Hyman argues that this is not because Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina lived in his days, nor is it to say that Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina was later, for there they said, “They laughed at it in the West,” at the words of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, and in the days of Rav Pappa the academies of the Land of Israel had already been destroyed. Rather the plain sense is that the rule “its majority is like its whole, by Torah law” was cited and fixed in the Gemara under the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, but these words had already been said in the days of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, and he raised a difficulty against it. This is clear.

In [Berakhot 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.52b.22) Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina cites Rav Huna, but Hyman judges the Rif’s reading more correct and proposes Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Chanina, who said several times in Rav Huna’s name. He suggests that “Rabbi Y.” was written and came to be read as Rabbi Yose. But we do find that he disagrees with Rav Huna, for which Hyman cites Ketubot 23a. His colleagues were all the great men of the generation, such as Rabbi Elazar, with whom he constantly disagrees, as in [Eruvin 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.103a.8-9), [Pesachim 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.19b.6), Zevachim 116 [no side supplied] and Maaser Sheni 4:3. He asked Rabbi Elazar, Niddah 22b. (כרוך חבירים ונשאר בחיקו, an unexplained parenthesis in the printed text.)[^14]

Rabbi Assi, as in [Bava Kamma 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.42b.7), where Rabbi Assi said: “This matter I heard from the mouth of a great man — and who is he? Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina.”
Rabbi Chelbo and Rabbi Avira, as in [Ketubot 112a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.112a.2).
Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim, as above. Their dispute: Eruvin 10:2.

Hyman writes: As we said above, he was a judge in his city, and so they said of him in [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.6-7) (in every place where they said) “They laughed at it in the West” — that is Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina. So too it is stated explicitly in [Eruvin 48a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.48a.1): Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina laughed at it (at Rabbi Chiyya’s words). In [Nazir 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.42a.4): “Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina challenged it — they laughed at it in the West”; and what the Tosafot there asked about the rule given in [Sanhedrin 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.17b.7). The expression “they laughed at it in the West” we find in [Beitzah 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.14a.2), [Yevamot 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.88a.12), [Bava Kamma 102b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.102b.6) and [Shevuot 34b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.34b.8). Besides being a judge, he led a great academy and had many students, as we find that Rabbi Abbahu said, “For me it was explained by Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina,” as in [Shabbat 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.94b.11) and [Bava Metzia 105a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.105a.11); [Pesachim 100a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.100a.3) gives Rabbi Abbahu in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina as an alternative to Rabbi Yirmeyah in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.[^15][^16]
Rabbi Avin teaches in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina in [Shabbat 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.94b.11).
Rabbi Ibo in his name, Pesachim 46 [no side supplied]; Rabbi Ami bar Ukva in his name, Ketubot 7:7.
Rabbi Bisna in his name, Shabbat 4:2.
Rabbi Berekhyah in his name, Kohelet Rabbah 5:10.
Rabbi Gurion in his name, Maaser Sheni 2:2.
Rabbi Hila in his name, Maaser Sheni, chapter 3, end of halakhah 2.
Rabbi Ze’ira in his name, Maaser Sheni, chapter 3, end of halakhah 2.
Rabbi Ze’ira bar Chama in his name, Yoma, beginning of chapter 5.
Rabbi Zerikan in his name, Pesachim 5:4.
Rabbi Chizkiyah in his name, Berakhot 8:7.
Rabbi Chiyya bar Bun in his name, Demai 3:4.

Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda teaches in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina, as in Sotah 6b in Hyman’s citation; Rav Chama bar Ukva teaches in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina in [Pesachim 52b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.52b.3), Sukkah 36b and [Kiddushin 72a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.72a.4); and Hyman proposes that reading there, 55a.[^17][^18]
Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi in his name, Bava Kamma, beginning of chapter 9.

Rabbi Yonatan ben Chaggai, Rabbi Yitzchak bar Maryon and Rabbi Azaryah said in his name that whoever eats his produce untithed [the reading suggested by the parallel] is as if he eats carcasses and torn animals. Hyman cites Tanchuma, Re’eh 16.
Rav Yehudah, his sister’s son, [Ketubot 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.49b.11).
Rabbi Yose the Galilean happened to come to his place, moved a lamp, and Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina was displeased, [Shabbat 46a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.46a.6).
Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose the Galilean said in his name, Berakhot, chapter 3, end of halakhah 1, the end of Kilayim, chapter 3, Shabbat 7:4 and Nazir 6:1.
Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun in his name, Terumot 9:2 and Nazir 4:5.
Rabbi Yose ben Pazi in his name, Shabbat, beginning of chapter 4.
Rabbi Yaakov son of Rabbi Bun in his name, Yevamot 10:8 and Kiddushin 1:2.

Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha in his name, Berakhot 8:7. With Rabbi Yirmeyah we find him in [Zevachim 108b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.108b.20-21): “Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina asked — Rabbi Yirmeyah said to him: It was taught.” Hyman explains that Rabbi Yirmeyah was already a great man of the generation in the days of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina’s activity.

Rabbi Nasa in his name, Bava Metzia, beginning of chapter 3. Mar Ukva bar Chama teaches in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina in [Zevachim 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.55b.4); Hyman reports Dikdukei Soferim’s reading as Rav Chama bar Ukva. Puga his attendant, [Bava Batra 90b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.90b.9).[^19]

Rabbi Krispa in his name, Shekalim 7:2. Ravin sent in his name, [Sanhedrin 51a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.51a.28) and [Chullin 101b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.101b.3). The Rabbis of Caesarea in his name, Shabbat 2:5 and 10:2.
Rabbi Tanchum bar Ilai in his name, Chagigah, chapter 2, beginning of halakhah 2.

Likewise we find “they say in the West in the name of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina,” as in [Bava Batra 80a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.80a.4) and Chullin 53a. Of his precious qualities, we find that he was very careful in matters of prayer, as in [Berakhot 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.6a.1), where he said that if two entered to pray and one finished praying first and waited for his fellow, he merits these blessings, etc. In Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:8 he said: “May my portion be among those who pray at the reddening of the sun” (in [Shabbat 118b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.118b.6) this saying is in the name of Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta, and Hyman judges the Jerusalem Talmud’s reading primary).[^20] And there, 8a,

he said: “When is a time of favor? At the hour when the congregation prays”; and there, 10a, his precious saying that a woman recognizes guests more than a man does. From his particular circumstances Hyman infers that he was wealthy, as in [Bava Batra 90b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.90b.9), where he said to Puga his attendant, “Store up produce for me for three years.”

He suffered grief over his children, as in [Taanit 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.13b.3-4): Rabbi Abba the Kohen said in the name of Rabbi Yose the Kohen: It happened that the sons of Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina died, and he bathed in cold water all seven days; and they said there that his mournings came in close succession (that his sons died one after another). Hyman writes: We do not find anywhere that he left sons or daughters, nor the time of his death.

An additional named-edition check now supplies a positive parallel: Midrash Tanchuma -- Torat Emet, Re’eh17, names Azaryah, Yonatan bar Chaggai and Yitzchak berabbi Maryon in Yose bar Chanina’s name and reads טבלים, untithed produce, in the comparison to carcasses and torn animals. Its preceding chapter16 does not contain that specific saying. Hyman’s supplied מבלים and Re’eh16 are retained, so this supports a provisional translation but does not settle his printed letters or locator. The earlier failed request remains preserved and is not evidence that the text was absent.

In Sanhedrin 30b, Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim seeks Rabbi Yose’s ordination before Rabbi Yochanan. In the Guggenheimer edition of Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 3:9, Rabbi Yonatan asks the question, Rabbi Yose points out Rabbi Shimon ben Yakim, and Shimon is told to come up (יקום לעיל). Guggenheimer explains this as taking a seat with the ordained judges. The proposal to read Yochanan for Yonatan and accept both ordinations is Hyman’s.

The title page and printed page 80, note 15, of Isaac Hirsch Weiss’s Dor Dor ve-Dorshav, part 3, confirm the reference. Weiss calls the Bavli reading corrupt and offers a possible reversal to agree with the Yerushalmi. Hyman cites Bava Kamma 117a; in the Davidson edition, the case judged by Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim and Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat appears at 117b. That case does not date either ordination.

The printed Hyman reads בל״ס, 'undoubtedly', where the supplied text reads כל״ס. Weiss’s main text on page 80 proposes an initial period of study in the south under Rabbi Chama. The Guggenheimer edition of Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 2:2 reports a teaching in Chama’s name. The identification of a teacher from that transmission and Hyman’s objection are historical arguments. The reported Zhitomir omission has not been collated here.

Hyman prints this parenthesis immediately after the citation to Niddah 22b. Its relation to the passage is unclear, so the supplied Hebrew is retained. In the Davidson edition, Rabbi Yose’s question to Rabbi Elazar about dry blood begins at 22a; the discussion crosses into 22b.

Hyman’s print appears to read מבלים and cites Re’eh 16. The Torat Emet edition at Re’eh 17 reads טבלים, 'untithed produce'. Its Hebrew names Rabbi Yonatan bar Chaggai and attributes the teaching to Yose bar Chananyah. The accompanying English renders the names as Johanan ben Haggai and Jose bar Hanina. The translation follows Hyman’s names.

The text consulted at [Berakhot 40b:24](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.40b.24) has Rabbi Yitzchak citing Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. It omits Rabbi Yose from this particular chain. [Berakhot 52b:22](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.52b.22) gives Rabbi Yose as the transmitter; [Seder HaDorot 1944](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1944&lang=en) reports the alternate name Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Chanina in the Rif and Rosh. Hyman’s reconstruction of the two lines at 40b remains his proposal.

In Nazir, the alternative to Rabbi Yochanan’s explanation is a teaching Rabbi Yose transmits in the name of Reish Lakish. In Bava Kamma, the opening dispute is followed by a proposed reversal of the two opinions, which Rava questions.

Rabbi Yose’s name at the end of [Nazir 28b:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.28b.11) introduces Reish Lakish’s explanation at [Nazir 29a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.29a.1). At [Ketubot 49b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.49b.4), Rabbi Ila’a cites Reish Lakish in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Chanina, the reading Hyman proposes.

The Yehudah attribution starts at [Eruvin 11a:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11a.19). The teaching about partitions continues at [Eruvin 11b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11b.1), the folio Hyman cites. Ketubot uses the same attribution for a different ruling.

[Arakhin 30b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Arakhin.30b.3) and Kiddushin name Rabbi Yose bar Rabbi Chanina for the Sabbatical-year teaching. Hyman suggests a different name and explains how the abbreviation could have been expanded. Tosafot records Rabbeinu Chananel’s alternative reading and Rabbeinu Tam’s proposal that two sages bore the name.

The consulted [Sifrei Devarim 1:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Devarim.1.18) likewise names Rabbi Yehudah for the ten trials. Rabbi Yose ben Dormaskit addresses him as “Yehudah Berabbi.” Hyman discusses a different reading of Sifrei.

In [Ketubot 63a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.63a.5), Rav Huna and Rabbi Yose give different explanations of marital rebellion. Eruvin and Pesachim name Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yose without assigning either opinion to either sage. The question about dry blood begins at [Niddah 22a:12-14](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.22a.12-14) and continues at [Niddah 22b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.22b.1), the folio Hyman cites.
Sanhedrin initially associates “they laughed at it in the West” with Rabbi Elazar, then reverses the association and gives Rabbi Yose bar Chanina.

Rabbi Chiyya’s teaching begins at [Eruvin 47b:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.47b.17) and Rabbi Yose’s reaction follows on the next folio. [Tosafot on Nazir 42a:4:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Nazir.42a.4.2) asks how the Western response in Nazir can be directed at Rabbi Yose’s objection when the Sanhedrin rule associates the formula with Rabbi Yose himself. Abbahu’s clarification in Shabbat continues at [Shabbat 95a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.95a.1).
[Sotah 7b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.7b.3) gives the Chiyya bar Gamda transmission on the verbal analogy for bringing the case before the Sanhedrin. Hyman cites Sotah 6b.

[Sukkah 37b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.37b.10) gives the same chain, with the title Rabbi for Chama, in the explanation of the ritual waving. Hyman cites Sukkah 36b. Kiddushin adds Abaye as an earlier link in the report.
[Heilprin’s entry on Puga](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2940&lang=en) also names him as Rabbi Yose’s attendant and cites Bava Batra 90b.

[Chullin 50b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.50b.5) and [Chullin 57a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.57a.6) give the Western reporting formula in Rabbi Yose’s name; Hyman cites Chullin 53a. The question about waiting for the other person to finish praying begins at [Berakhot 5b:27](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.5b.27). [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.4.1.19) names Rabbi Yose ben Chanina for the sunset prayer. The consulted Shabbat has “Rabbi Yose.” Hyman identifies him there as Rabbi Yose ben Chalafta and prefers the Jerusalem Talmud attribution.
